services: Custom Software Development AI/ML Engineering Data Engineering System Architecture
about_client:
The client is an enterprise organization seeking a scalable AI-driven data access solution
to unify document-based knowledge and structured database records for faster analytics
and operational decision-making.
story:
The client engaged FiftyFive for a full-cycle custom software development engagement
to build a unified AI query system. The objective was to enable seamless access to both
unstructured PDF documents and structured PostgreSQL data through a single natural
language interface. Initially designed as an agentic AI architecture, the solution was
restructured into a function-based orchestration model to align with delivery timelines
and MVP goals. FiftyFive handled architecture design, AI engineering, orchestration
logic, and backend integration.
challenges:
● Integrating unstructured document retrieval with structured database querying in
a single system.
● Implementing semantic search over PDF documents using vector embeddings.
● Translating natural language queries into executable SQL statements.
● Designing dynamic query classification without stateful agent memory.
● Reducing latency and compute overhead while maintaining response accuracy.
● Delivering a production-ready MVP within strict time constraints.
solution:
● Built a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline using Vertex AI
text-embedding-004 for embedding generation.
● Implemented Milvus as the vector database for semantic chunk storage and
retrieval.
● Integrated Gemini Pro for document re-ranking and response generation.
● Developed an NL2SQL module using Gemini Pro to convert natural language into
PostgreSQL queries.
● Executed SQL queries directly on PostgreSQL and returned structured tabular
outputs with explanations.
● Designed a lightweight function-based orchestration layer using
prompt-engineered classification logic to route queries between RAG and SQL
pipelines.
● Replaced planned agentic architecture with modular function orchestration to
reduce system complexity and improve deployment speed.
outcome:
FiftyFive delivered a unified AI-powered query system that reduced architectural
complexity, minimized compute overhead, and accelerated MVP deployment. The
function-based orchestration improved query response speed by eliminating agent
memory overhead, enabling faster data access across structured and unstructured
sources. The modular architecture supports future agent integration, providing
scalability while maintaining operational efficiency and cost control.

project_name: AI Governance Sandbox for Credit Risk
project_brief: Sorai Designed and deployed an AI auditing sandbox to validate credit risk models under macroeconomic stress and fraud scenarios.
project_description: Sorai Designed and deployed an AI auditing sandbox to validate credit risk models under macroeconomic stress and fraud scenarios.
services: Custom Software Development AI Governance & Auditing Predictive Modeling Fraud Detection Risk Analytics
about_client:
The client is an England-based financial technology company developing AI-driven
platforms for regulated financial institutions, focusing on credit risk, underwriting
intelligence, and governance frameworks for high-risk decision systems.
story:
The client engaged FiftyFive as its technology partner to design and build a
regulatory-grade AI governance sandbox for auditing credit risk models. The
engagement covered full-cycle custom software development, including predictive
modeling, macroeconomic simulation, fraud validation, and governance reporting. A
dedicated AI and data engineering team delivered an end-to-end platform to evaluate a
Probability of Default (PD) model used in underwriting. The objective was to enable
regulator-aligned validation under long-term macroeconomic stress without data
leakage.
challenges:
● Limited transparency and borrower-level explainability in PD models
● Unstructured fairness and demographic bias assessment
● Absence of long-horizon macroeconomic stress testing framework
● Inability to simulate income volatility, expense inflation, and rate shocks
● Weak fraud validation across uploaded financial documents
● No consolidated audit reporting for AI governance readiness
solution:
● Engineered an XGBoost-based PD model using DSCR and DTI indicators
● Integrated SHAP for borrower-level feature attribution and model interpretability
● Implemented demographic fairness and bias evaluation pipelines
● Built a What-If simulation engine modeling salary growth, rent increases,
subscription creep, and interest rate hikes
● Integrated 15–20 year projections using inflation, wage growth, unemployment,
and interest rate indicators
● Deployed Isolation Forest for anomaly detection under stress scenarios
● Developed document intelligence engine with OCR preprocessing, MRZ
validation, checksum logic, and image forensics
● Designed composite fraud scoring framework combining OCR confidence, rule
violations, and image penalties
outcome:
The platform consolidated fairness, explainability, robustness, and fraud validation into
a single audit-ready environment. Borrower-level SHAP explanations improved
underwriting traceability and transparency. Long-term macroeconomic simulations
validated model resilience across inflation, wage, unemployment, and interest rate
shocks, reducing hidden systemic risk exposure. Fraud detection accuracy improved
through structured document intelligence and anomaly modeling. The solution elevated
AI governance maturity and established a scalable foundation for compliance-driven
deployment of high-risk financial AI systems.

services: Custom Software Development – Backend architecture, SaaS platform engineering AI/ML Engineering – Legal RAG pipeline, gap detection engine, LLM-based drafting Cloud Engineering – AWS GPU deployment, infrastructure optimization Security & Multi-Tenancy Architecture – Tenant allowlists, applicability enforcement Data Engineering – Embedding pipeline, indexing workflow, validation systems
about_client:
The client is a Sweden-based LegalTech company building an AI-driven SaaS compliance
platform that automates policy analysis, regulatory tracking, and license workflows for
organizations and legal professionals.
story:
The client engaged FiftyFive as a dedicated custom software development partner to
replace manual, clause-level compliance reviews with a scalable AI-powered system. The
mandate included full-cycle backend engineering, AI pipeline design, GPU optimization,
and secure multi-tenant SaaS architecture. FiftyFive deployed a focused engineering
team covering AI/ML, backend, cloud, and security to deliver a production-grade,
auditable compliance automation platform.
challenges:
● Manual clause-by-clause policy-to-law matching and remediation drafting
● CPU-bound inference cycles (~40 minutes per policy run)
● Legal knowledge base indexing cycles taking ~1 week
● Vector index and metadata store inconsistencies causing mapping drift
● Missing provenance and unreliable legal excerpt hydration
● Multi-tenant law applicability risks without strict customer scoping
● Non-deterministic outputs and unstable retrieval results
solution:
● Architected a GPU-accelerated Legal RAG pipeline deployed on AWS g6.xlarge
(NVIDIA L4)
● Designed a tiered multi-layer vector indexing architecture (L0/L2/L3/L4) for recall
and precision balance
● Implemented structured ingestion → normalization → chunking → embedding
→ indexing → validation pipeline
● Migrated similarity search and embedding workloads to GPU for latency
reduction
● Built backend job-artifact framework producing deterministic, auditable run
outputs
● Developed two-pass engine: deterministic gap detection (Pass A) and bounded
OpenAI-based drafting (Pass B)
● Enforced database-driven tenant allowlists with strict applicability controls
● Standardized canonical JSON outputs with structured fields (issue, rationale,
confidence, spans, provenance)
outcome:
Policy-to-law validation time reduced from ~40 minutes (CPU) to ~3 minutes (GPU),
enabling near real-time compliance checks and higher processing throughput. Legal RAG
rebuild cycles improved from ~1 week to ~3 hours, accelerating regulatory updates and
product releases. Automated gap detection significantly reduced manual lawyer
workload while preserving evidence traceability. Deterministic artifacts and strict tenant
scoping strengthened auditability, enterprise trust, and platform scalability for growth
across jurisdictions.
